cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort the cafe before we open. That chair wobbles; let's dismantle the chairs and check the joints.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I checked. It's just that floorboard. The chairs are fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good testing. We'll keep the chairs and lift the boards. Tell me which area you want clear first; I'll work around you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We open in twenty minutes. I need the counter accessible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll close for renovations and move the counter somewhere better. You choose where service should start; I'll plan the new queue around it. Much easier once the floor's up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes charge before opening; A3 adopts B diagnosis and grants area preference, then A5 grants service-location choice while broadening the work to closure and counter move.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 localized floor problem causes A3 floor work; B4 opening/counter need causes A5 closure and service redesign.

relationship.evidence: B2 has tested the chairs and B4 needs a usable workplace; A recruits that knowledge into the project.

heightening.evidence: A5 resolves the inconvenience of renovation before opening by embracing a longer closure and larger renovation.

specificity.evidence: A1 cafe and B4 twenty-minute opening make the disruption meaningful.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 new queue is a concrete broader arrangement tied to counter access, not a detached joke.
